## B. Account Terms

**Short version:** _Personal Accounts and Organizations get different admin controls; a real human has to create your Account; you've got to be 13 or over; you've got to give us a working email address; and you can't have more than one free Account. You and you alone are on the hook for your Account and anything that happens while you're signed in to it or using it. Keeping your Account secure is your job._

### 1. Account Controls

* Users. Subject to these Terms, you keep the final say on admin control over your Personal Account and the Content in it.

* Organizations. The "owner" of an Organization set up under these Terms has the final say on admin control over that Organization and the Content in it. Within the Service, an owner can manage which Users get access to the Organization's data and projects. An Organization can have more than one owner, but at least one Personal Account has to be named as an owner of an Organization. If you're the owner of an Organization under these Terms, we hold you responsible for whatever gets done on or through that Organization.

### 2. Required Information

You've got to give us a working email address to finish signing up. Anything else we ask for, like your real name, is up to you, unless you're accepting these terms on behalf of a legal entity (in which case we need more info about that entity) or you go for a [paid Account](#l-payment), in which case we'll need a bit more for billing.

### 3. Account Requirements

We've got a few simple rules for Accounts on GitHub's Service.
* You've got to be a human to create an Account. Accounts signed up by "bots" or other automated means aren't allowed. We do allow machine accounts, though:
* A machine account is an Account set up by an individual human who accepts the Terms on the Account's behalf, gives a working email address, and wears the blame for what it does. A machine account is only for doing automated yakka. Any number of users can tell a machine account what to do, but at the end of the day the owner of the Account is the one responsible for what the machine does. You can have no more than one free machine account on top of your free Personal Account.
* One person or legal entity can have no more than one free Account (if you want to run a machine account as well, that's fine, but it can only be used for running a machine).
* You've got to be 13 or older. We're stoked to see beaut young coders getting fired up about learning to program, but we have to follow United States law. GitHub doesn't aim our Service at kids under 13, and we don't allow any Users under 13 on our Service. If we find out a User is under 13, we'll [shut that User's Account down straight away](#m-cancellation-and-termination). If you live in a country outside the United States, your country's minimum age might be higher; if so, it's on you to follow your country's laws.
* Your login can only be used by one person: no sharing one login around a group of people. A paid Organization can only give access to as many Personal Accounts as your subscription allows.
* You can't use GitHub in breach of the export control or sanctions laws of the United States or anywhere else whose laws apply. You can't use GitHub if you are, or are working on behalf of, a [Specially Designated National (SDN)](https://www.treasury.gov/resource-center/sanctions/SDN-List/Pages/default.aspx) or a person caught by similar blocking or denied party bans run by a U.S. government agency. GitHub may let people in certain sanctioned countries or territories use certain GitHub services under U.S. government authorisations. For more info, have a look at our [Export Controls policy](/site-policy/other-site-policies/github-and-trade-controls).
